_comment: Watchlist for competitor outlier mining (/competitors/mine). Each week the miner pulls each channel's recent SHORTS, finds the ones that beat that channel's OWN median views (an outlier - a breakout, normalized per channel so a small channel is judged fairly against a giant one), and distills the transferable topic/angle patterns into competitor_signals.json, which the topic generator reads as inspiration. It NEVER copies titles. Edit this list freely: add a channel with either a channel_id (UC...) or a handle (@name) - at least one is required; the miner resolves and validates each at runtime and reports any it could not resolve. You can also override this whole list without a code edit via the COMPETITOR_CHANNELS env var (a comma-separated list of @handles/UC ids, set as a GitHub secret; applies on the next deploy). IMPORTANT LESSON LEARNED: a channel having a big subscriber count or a matching description does NOT mean it is currently active - several previously-listed channels (large subs, right format) turned out to have gone dormant 1-3+ years ago and always scanned at 0 recent_shorts. Every channel below was verified by opening its actual Shorts tab on YouTube and checking the most recent upload date at the time of writing (2026-10-05, after the switch to the social-psychology niche) - each had posted within the last few days. If a channel here goes quiet, drop it and re-verify a replacement the same way (check upload recency, not just subs/description) rather than trusting a listicle or stats site.
